Index corruption or unstaged drift: ls-files and diff both succeed against the index
Ref/HEAD or tree/commit damage: rev-parse HEAD:path resolves normally to the blob ID

The configuration is not missing at all: the file exists on disk, is tracked, clean, and named in the HEAD tree. evidenceChain: test -f exits 0 → file present on disk; filesystem layer intact.
git ls-files --error-unmatch exits 0 and git diff --exit-code exits 0 → index tracks the path and worktree matches it.

Because blob IDs are content-addressed and the tracked file is clean, the on-disk copy should re-hash to b7a1…, enabling exact, verifiable regeneration.
firstTwoActions: Verify content-addressed identity: run `git hash-object services/payments/config.toml` and confirm the output equals b7a1b7a1b7a1b7a1b7a1b7a1b7a1b7a1b7a1b7a1. This proves the intact working-tree copy is byte-identical to the missing blob (no unverified data involved).

Only if the hash matches, regenerate the object: `git hash-object -w services/payments/config.toml` (writes into the shared store; self-verifying because the resulting ID must equal b7a1…). Then confirm with `git cat-file -e b7a1…^{blob}` and re-run `git fsck --full` to check whether this was the only missing object before re-running the build wrapper.

Git index / untracked-file problem — ls-files --error-unmatch and clean git diff show it is tracked and unmodified.
HEAD tree / bad commit or wrong branch — rev-parse resolves the path to a concrete blob ID.
Wrapper or repo configuration error — every layer above the object store checks out; the message text is a red herring.
Worktree linkage breakage — .git gitdir pointer resolves and a second worktree with the same common dir fails identically.
Fetching from remote to repair — network to the remote is unavailable in the incident window.
Recreating/replacing the config file, resetting worktrees, git gc, or recloning — destructive/forbidden and unnecessary; the clean tracked copy can regenerate the exact blob.
Copying an object file from elsewhere unverified — forbidden; hash-object regeneration is inherently hash-verified instead.
